ON THE ELLIPTIC CURVE: the section of the non-trivial flat line of order two with one pole allowed at p has exactly one zero, at a half-period that is not p (theta_3/theta_1: both multipliers -1, residue non-zero, zeros minus poles 0 in a cell), so in Hom degree two the two maps have divisors 2p and p + q and their common divisor is p, 2p or p + q. THE LOCAL COMPLEX: for A --(f0, f1)--> B + C --(-f1, f0)--> D the first map is injective and both cohomology modules have the length of the common divisor (exact linear algebra on truncated polynomial spaces: 1 in the generic case, 2 on each axis, 0 for a control with no common zero). THE POLE TEST gives the degrees -2, 0, 0, 2. THE CORNER REDUCTION: the matrix with three pivots and one corner is an isomorphism plus the corner, the corner's products with the pivot homotopy vanish in both orders, and the two-factor Koszul complex has cohomology 1, 2, 1 when both corners vanish and none otherwise. THE COUNT: Riemann-Roch gives 3 or 2 per gauge component at the origin; off it the kernel is the common divisor's length; over the 128 that is 18, 16, 8, or 16, 16, 8 with no trivial middle line. THE SECONDARY MAP: after the common factor is removed the sequence 0 -> A(p) -> B + C -> D(-p) -> 0 has degrees -1, 0, 0, 1 with one-dimensional outer cohomology, so the map H1(A) -> H0(D) between two-dimensional spaces has rank 1 when both middle lines are acyclic, which is also what the two counts leave for it; its formula F0 G F1 - F1 G F0 is closed and the opposite sign is not, and it removes exactly its rank from the total cohomology (a finite graded model, where a common linear factor of the two quadrics gives rank 1 and one surviving class); the second-order Schur coefficient (a finite model)
